# Revenue Bench

> Specialized recruitment for the revenue engine. Revenue Bench finds, assesses, places, and coaches sales talent that performs: sellers, sales leaders, enablement, and RevOps. Not just resumes that interview well.

Revenue Bench is a founder-led sales recruitment firm launched in 2026 by Carlos Garrido and Steve Swanston. Every placement is assessed with the Objective Management Group (OMG) sales-specific assessment, arrives with a training refresher, gets a dedicated onboarding coach for the first 90 days, and is backed by a 90-day replacement guarantee. The firm serves high-growth and private-equity-backed companies, and maintains a pre-vetted "bench" of revenue talent so clients can hire without building their own pipeline.

Founder track record (stated separately, never combined): Carlos Garrido, an investment banker and growth advisor for more than 30 years, has supported $3B+ in client revenue growth and $6B+ in client exits. Steve Swanston brings $500M+ in exits and an OMG Certified Partner pedigree. Revenue Bench is a sister firm to Performance Edge, Swanston Growth Advisors, and Best Sales Team Training.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://revenuebench.io/): What Revenue Bench does, and why operators, not recruiters, find revenue.
- [For Employers](https://revenuebench.io/for-employers): How companies hire revenue talent that performs, with OMG assessment, a training refresher, a 90-day onboarding coach, and a replacement guarantee.
- [How It Works](https://revenuebench.io/how-it-works): The six-step search with a stage-by-stage timeline (typical durations, owners, and the standard cleared before each stage advances). Define the role, source from the bench, assess with OMG, present a true shortlist, place and train, then coach for 90 days. Kickoff to shortlist is commonly 2 to 4 weeks when the bench covers the role.
- [Private Equity](https://revenuebench.io/private-equity): Recruiting and ramping the sellers and sales leaders a value-creation plan assumes, across a portfolio.
- [For Candidates](https://revenuebench.io/for-candidates): How revenue professionals get on the bench, assessed objectively, placed into system-led teams, and coached through their first 90 days. No cost to candidates.
- [About](https://revenuebench.io/about): The founders and the operator network behind every search.
- [Contact](https://revenuebench.io/contact): Tell us about the role you are filling, or that you want on the bench. A founder replies within one business day.

## Insights and guides

- [Why Sales Hires Fail: What 2.4 Million Assessments Show](https://revenuebench.io/guides/why-sales-hires-fail): Original analysis by co-founder Steve Swanston through Swanston Growth Advisors, a Certified Partner of Objective Management Group. Five failure patterns across the largest sales-specific dataset, the numbers behind each, and how to hire against them.
- [Should You Promote Your Best Rep Into Sales Management?](https://revenuebench.io/guides/should-you-promote-your-best-rep): Original analysis by Steve Swanston: in OMG's evaluation of 44,493 sales managers only 9% are strong in all three coaching qualities, selling and coaching are different measurable skills, and the four-move decision including the dual-track alternative.
- [The Private Equity Operating Partner's Sales-Hiring Playbook](https://revenuebench.io/guides/private-equity-sales-hiring-playbook): The four-phase governance model for sales talent across the hold (diligence, first 100 days, the build, exit preparation), the turnover math a portfolio multiplies (9% vs 33% first-year turnover in OMG's 2024 validation data), and the standards to demand from any search partner.
- [How to Replace a VP of Sales Confidentially](https://revenuebench.io/guides/confidential-vp-of-sales-replacement): Confirming the replacement decision on assessment evidence, a six-stage confidentiality protocol (the risk, who is read in, and the control at each stage), and how assessment-led selection keeps a contained search high-fit. Cites OMG's 2024 validation data (9% vs 33% first-year turnover, 72% top half).
- [Sales Recruiter Fees: Contingency, Retained, and What You Pay For](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-recruiter-fees): The three fee models (contingency, retained, container/engaged) compared by who carries the search risk, exclusivity, and the incentive each creates. Why the headline percentage is the wrong number to shop, since a wrong hire costs far more (DePaul: ~$115,000 fully loaded; Revenue Bench working figure $200,000 to $250,000), and how a 90-day replacement guarantee and an OMG assessment change the economics. Cites OMG's 2024 validation data (72% top half, 9% vs 33% turnover).
- [Sales-Team Due Diligence Before the Deal Closes](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-team-due-diligence): The pre-LOI sales-team checklist a deal team can run from the data room, public sources, and management meetings before exclusivity, with the red flag for each area. What a sales-specific assessment of the leader and the quota-carrying team adds in the confirmatory window between the LOI and close, and the distribution to expect (OMG: 6% Elite, 11% Strong, 33% Serviceable, 50% Weak). The turnover cost math that re-prices the model (9% vs 33% first-year turnover in OMG's 2024 validation data; DePaul: ~$49,508 average, ~$115,000 fully loaded), and the three outcomes: price it, plan for it, or pass.
- [The First 100 Days: Rebuilding a Portfolio Company's Sales Team](https://revenuebench.io/guides/first-100-days-portfolio-sales-team): The post-close decision sequence for an operating partner and a portfolio company CEO, published as a six-window table: the decision that closes in each window, the evidence it rests on, who owns it, and what running it late costs. Why the sales leader decision closes inside 30 days before any seat change below it, what a team baseline answers that a performance history cannot (OMG: 6% Elite, 11% Strong, 33% Serviceable, 50% Weak), why organization design closes before a search opens, and the written terms the first replacements run under. Cites OMG's evaluation of 44,493 sales managers (9% strong in all three coaching qualities, 80% more elite salespeople) and OMG's 2024 validation data (9% vs 33% first-year turnover, 72% top half), with DePaul turnover costs (~$49,508 average, ~$115,000 fully loaded) and CSO Insights on ramp time.
- [How to Evaluate a Sales Recruitment Agency](https://revenuebench.io/guides/how-to-evaluate-a-sales-recruitment-agency): An eight-criteria scorecard for vetting any sales recruiter: assessment method, written guarantee terms, specialization, who does the work, fee clarity. Honest about when Revenue Bench is not the fit.
- [How Placement Guarantees Work in Sales Recruitment](https://revenuebench.io/guides/placement-guarantees-explained): The three guarantee types, the void conditions, what to demand in writing, and Revenue Bench's own published terms: 90 days from the hire's start date, one free re-run of the search, no conditions. Includes a six-stage walkthrough of what happens when a guarantee is used, from the client's decision through the re-run search to the replacement hire's first day, and an honest account of what a replacement guarantee does not cover.
- [When a Sales Hire Is Not Working Out: Cut, Coach, or Replace](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-hire-not-working-out): Triage for a struggling hire: wrong profile vs no process vs no onboarding, the check for each, the documented cost of waiting, and the recovery path.
- [The True Cost of a Bad Sales Hire](https://revenuebench.io/guides/cost-of-a-bad-sales-hire): The $200,000 to $250,000 working figure for a revenue-role mis-hire, plus the vacancy ledger, arithmetic that prices an open sales territory from the company's own quota, pipeline, ramp, and team inputs.
- [The 6% Problem](https://revenuebench.io/guides/the-6-percent-problem): What the largest database of assessed salespeople shows. Only 6% are elite and half are weak.
- [Sales Assessment vs Interview: What Each Screen Catches](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-assessment-vs-interview): The division of labor in sales hiring: what the OMG screen measures (predictive validity in the 95 percent range, OMG's figure), what interviews alone can verify, and a decision table routing each hiring question to the screen built to decide it. Includes OMG's 2024 outcome figures, era-labeled, and the sequence Revenue Bench runs.
- [Will to Sell: Why Drive Is a Hiring Decision](https://revenuebench.io/guides/will-to-sell): OMG's construct explained for hiring teams: the five markers (Desire, Commitment, Motivation, Responsibility, Outlook), the before-and-after training study of 5,331 salespeople showing Will to Sell moved 0 to 6 percent while tactical skills jumped (OMG's data, labeled), and the five-marker table with what weak looks like in the first 90 days. Drive is screened before the hire; skill is coached after it.
- [How to Assess a Salesperson Beyond the Resume](https://revenuebench.io/guides/how-to-assess-a-salesperson): The four traits that predict performance, and how to measure them objectively.
- [The Sales Leader Interview Scorecard](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-leader-interview-scorecard): The pre-hire scoring instrument for VP of Sales, Head of Sales, and CRO interviews: seven weighted dimensions with anchored 1-to-5 answer patterns (coaching evidence and team building weighted heaviest), an independent-scoring protocol with advancement thresholds, and two disqualifiers that end a candidacy regardless of the total. The dimensions, weights, and thresholds are Revenue Bench's own instrument, labeled as such; the interview scores what only interviews decide, with drive and Sales DNA measured by assessment beforehand.
- [The Account Executive Interview Scorecard](https://revenuebench.io/guides/account-executive-interview-scorecard): The companion instrument for individual-contributor seller hires: seven weighted dimensions with anchored 1-to-5 answer patterns (verifiable track record and prospecting discipline weighted heaviest), an independent-scoring protocol with a worked weighted-total example, two disqualifiers, a printable score sheet with evidence fields, and defensibility guidance for using a cut-score instrument. The dimensions, weights, and thresholds are Revenue Bench's own instrument, labeled as such.
- [Reference Checks for Sales Hires](https://revenuebench.io/guides/reference-checks-for-sales-hires): The consent-run protocol for the final screen: a five-step consent sequence with the current manager off the list by default, ten questions across verification, performance context, working reality, and the closing questions, each with what a weak answer sounds like, and the boundaries: many employers confirm only title and dates, a policy-limited answer is recorded as unavailable rather than negative, and references cannot decide future performance in a different role. The question set is Revenue Bench's own protocol, labeled as such.
- [The Founder's First Sales Hires: #1 Through #3](https://revenuebench.io/guides/founders-first-sales-hires): The hiring-sequence map for founder-led companies: what must exist before hires #1, #2, and #3, what each hire owns, what the founder's job becomes at each step, and the failure pattern each hire meets when its precondition is skipped. Hire #1 tests transferability, hire #2 proves the process travels, hire #3 marks the team threshold. Built on the who-runs-the-system progression from Carlos Garrido's Building a Scalable Sales Team masterclass; the map is Revenue Bench's own framework, labeled as such.
- [CRO, VP of Sales, or Fractional: Choosing the Sales Leadership Model](https://revenuebench.io/guides/choosing-a-sales-leadership-model): The stage-to-model matrix: five company stages defined by observable operating conditions (who closes, whether the motion repeats, how many functions share revenue responsibility), the model that fits each, what that leader must own, when each model breaks, and the trigger to change model. Includes the failure patterns (the CRO hired too early, the VP hired too late, the fractional engagement treated as permanent) and the honest option most guides skip: no full-time hire yet. The matrix is Revenue Bench's own framework, labeled as such.
- [How to Hire a VP of Sales or Sales Manager](https://revenuebench.io/guides/how-to-hire-a-vp-of-sales): Why not to default to your top seller, the four red flags, and the 30/60/90-day scorecard.
- [The 90-Day Onboarding Plan That Reaches Quota](https://revenuebench.io/guides/90-day-sales-onboarding-plan): The cadence and coaching that turns a new hire into a quota carrier by day 90.
- [Building a Sales Talent Bench](https://revenuebench.io/guides/building-a-sales-talent-bench): How to source revenue talent before you need it.
- [Sales Compensation Benchmarks for 2026](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-compensation-benchmarks-2026): OTE by role, base and variable mix, quota, and accelerators.
- [When to Use a Sales Recruitment Partner vs In-House](https://revenuebench.io/guides/sales-recruiter-vs-in-house): Which roles justify a specialist, and how one earns its fee.
- [All Insights](https://revenuebench.io/guides): The full guide library.
